source_metadata.question_text: How many distinct values can be obtained from <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> by inserting parentheses (no rearranging of factors)?
source_metadata.explanation: Only the placement of the <math><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> changes the value. The four possibilities are <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn></math>, <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></math>, <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>122</mn></math>, and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>121</mn></math>.

derived_analysis.sub_skill: Counting distinct evaluation results under different parenthesizations; associativity awareness
derived_analysis.problem_family: Parentheses placement and evaluation-order effects on mixed operations (multiplication and addition); counting distinct numeric outcomes from different binary tree parenthesizations
solve_strategy: Enumerate all structurally different full parenthesizations (binary trees) consistent with the given operand order that can change where the +1 is applied.
Identify which parenthesizations actually change the numerical effect of the +1 (i.e., whether +1 is inside some product factor or applied after all multiplications).
Evaluate each distinct relevant parenthesization numerically and collect distinct results.
Count distinct outcomes and map to appropriate answer choice.
derived_analysis.reasoning_pattern: Case analysis over possible parenthesizations combined with application of associativity of multiplication and non-distributivity of addition over multiplication (so placing +1 inside a product changes the result).
logic_invariants: Multiplication is associative: grouping of pure products without addition does not change the product value.
Addition is not distributively equivalent to arbitrary regroupings: (a·b)+1 generally differs from a·(b+1).
Operands' order (sequence of factors) is fixed; only grouping (parentheses) may change evaluation order.
Distinct parenthesizations may lead to equal numeric results in special cases (e.g., zeros or ones), but with given operands they can be distinct.
changeable_parameters: Number of multiplicative factors before the +1 (length of factor chain).
Values of the multiplicative factors (positive integers, could include 0 or 1).
Position of the +1 relative to the chain (always at the end in this template, but could be inserted after other factors).
Type of operator used in the chain (e.g., multiplication, exponentiation) and position of the additive term.
Whether multiple additions are present instead of a single +1.
parameter_constraints: Operands' sequence must remain fixed (no reordering allowed).
Parentheses may be inserted only to change evaluation order; binary operation semantics apply.
For the typical problem flavor, factors are positive integers >1 to avoid degenerate equalities caused by 0 or 1.
Exactly one additive term (like +1) is present to keep the counting tractable unless intentionally varied.
derived_analysis.answer_format: integer (count of distinct numeric values); for multiple-choice instances: option letter corresponding to that count
rendering_notes: Preserve original <math>...</math> MathML tags exactly in question text and choices.
When generating new variants, use MathML for inline numeric expressions to match source format.
Ensure parentheses are rendered clearly (use explicit parentheses in MathML when describing grouping).
risk_flags: Counting all Catalan-number parenthesizations instead of only those that change the location of the addition (overcount).
Assuming associativity of addition across multiplication (i.e., thinking grouping can't change value) — leads to undercounting.
Including degenerate parameter choices like 0 or 1 that collapse multiple parenthesizations to the same numeric result, changing answer key.
Misreading 'no rearranging of factors' and allowing commutativity to produce new orders.

changeable_parameters.name: number_of_multiplicative_factors
changeable_parameters.role: How many multiplicative operands appear before the additive term

changeable_parameters.name: values_of_factors_in_order
changeable_parameters.role: Ordered list of multiplicative factor values (do not reorder)
changeable_parameters.suggested_range: each integer 2-9 (avoid 0 or 1 unless allow_degenerate_factors_flag true)
constraints: prefer integers >1 to avoid degenerate equalities

changeable_parameters.name: additive_term_value_k
changeable_parameters.role: The integer added (e.g., the '+1' in the source)
constraints: can be varied to change distinct-result counts

changeable_parameters.name: position_of_additive_term
changeable_parameters.role: Which grouping places the additive term inside a product factor vs applied after multiplication (affects counting)
changeable_parameters.current_value: attached to last operand (as '+k' after last factor)
changeable_parameters.suggested_range: attach inside factor i via grouping or apply after all multiplications
constraints: must not reorder operands; position refers to grouping only
generator should enumerate placements that are achievable by parenthesization

changeable_parameters.name: allow_degenerate_factors_flag
changeable_parameters.role: Whether factors may include 0 or 1 (degenerate cases permitted)
constraints: if true, many parenthesizations may evaluate to same result; generator must recalc distinct counts accordingly

changeable_parameters.name: number_of_additive_terms
constraints: if >1, problem complexity increases; define precisely where each additive term is placed

generation_guidance: must_change: Each generated instance must change at least one structural element: number_of_multiplicative_factors OR position_of_additive_term OR values_of_factors_in_order (not just cosmetic number substitution).

allowed_variations: Change the count of factors (recommended 3-6), change factor values (integers >1), change additive k, move +k via grouping to different factor positions, optionally allow one additive term only unless explicitly varying template.

forbidden_variations: Do not reorder factors (commutativity not allowed), do not silently allow 0 or 1 as factors unless allow_degenerate_factors_flag is explicitly set, do not replace multiplication with other operators unless defining a new template.

instance_acceptance_rule: Novelty — new instance must not be identical in both factor sequence and additive-position parenthesization set to any example in known_values; either factor list or number_of_factors or additive placement must differ.

instance_acceptance_rule: Mathematical validity — for the chosen parameters, enumerate all full parenthesizations of the fixed operand sequence, evaluate each exactly, and compute the set of distinct numeric results; the reported answer equals the size of that set.

instance_acceptance_rule: Degeneracy check — if allow_degenerate_factors_flag is false, reject instances containing factor 0 or 1; if true, require explanation note that degeneracy may reduce distinct counts.
validation_hint: After generation, compute Catalan(n-1) parenthesizations for n factors and verify the distinct-results count is correctly determined by evaluation (not by counting trees).
distractors_guidance: For multiple-choice, construct distractors that are off-by-one from the true count and the Catalan number for n-1 to catch common errors (under/overcounting).
presentation: Use MathML (<math>...</math>) for inline expressions and explicit parentheses for each parenthesization shown in explanation.
fallback_generation_hint: Vary the number of multiplicative factors to 3–5 and keep small integer factors (2–6) with additive k between 1 and 3; enumerate parenthesizations and compute distinct evaluation results to produce a valid question and answer.
